mathematical_concepts.description: When the multiplier decreases by 1, the product changes by the value of the multiplicand
The absolute value of the product depends only on the absolute values of the factors
Zero serves as the boundary between positive and negative products
Using integers to represent direction, status, or change in various contexts

practice_questions.question: What is the product of (-4) × 3?
practice_questions.explanation: When multiplying a negative number by a positive number, the product is negative. (-4) × 3 = -12

practice_questions.question: What is the result of (-6) × (-5)?
practice_questions.explanation: When both the multiplier and multiplicand are negative, the product is positive. (-6) × (-5) = 30

practice_questions.question: In the pattern 3 × 4 = 12, 2 × 4 = 8, 1 × 4 = 4, 0 × 4 = 0, what comes next?
practice_questions.explanation: The product decreases by 4 each time. Following the pattern: 0 - 4 = -4. So (-1) × 4 = -4

practice_questions.question: If 5 × (-3) = -15, what is (-5) × (-3)?
practice_questions.explanation: When the multiplicand is negative and we change the multiplier from positive to negative, the product becomes positive. (-5) × (-3) = 15

practice_questions.question: What happens to the product when the multiplier decreases by 1 in the sequence where multiplicand is -4?
practice_questions.explanation: When the multiplicand is negative (-4), the product increases by the absolute value of the multiplicand (4) as the multiplier decreases by 1. This is the inverse pattern compared to positive multiplicands.

realworld_examples.title: Temperature Changes
realworld_examples.scenario: A freezing laboratory needs to lower its temperature by 5°C every hour for preservation purposes.
realworld_examples.problem: If the lab starts at 15°C and the temperature drops by 5°C per hour, what will the temperature be after 4 hours?
realworld_examples.solution: We can model this as: Initial temperature + (Number of hours × Temperature change per hour)
realworld_examples.application: The laboratory will reach -5°C after 4 hours. This shows how multiplying positive time by negative temperature change gives us the total drop.
realworld_examples.real_world_relevance: Used in climate control, refrigeration, weather forecasting

realworld_examples.title: Financial Transactions - Debt Payments
realworld_examples.scenario: Ravi owes ₹300 to each of his 5 friends. We represent debts as negative numbers.
realworld_examples.problem: What is Ravi's total debt situation?
realworld_examples.solution: We model each debt as -300 and multiply by the number of friends.
realworld_examples.application: Ravi has a total debt of ₹1,500. Positive number of friends multiplied by negative debt (per friend) gives total negative financial position.
realworld_examples.real_world_relevance: Used in accounting, budgeting, loan calculations

realworld_examples.title: Elevator in Mining Shaft
realworld_examples.scenario: A mining elevator descends at 3 meters per minute. Downward movement is represented as negative.
realworld_examples.problem: If the elevator moves down for 8 minutes, what is its position relative to ground level (0 meters)?
realworld_examples.solution: Time (positive) × Speed with direction (negative) = Total displacement
realworld_examples.application: The elevator is 24 meters below ground level. This shows how positive time multiplied by negative speed (downward) gives negative position (below ground).
realworld_examples.real_world_relevance: Used in mining, construction, elevation mapping

realworld_examples.title: Reversing Video Playback
realworld_examples.scenario: A video player is in rewind mode, going backward at 2× speed. We represent backward as negative.
realworld_examples.problem: If you rewind for 6 seconds, how much video time do you go back?
realworld_examples.solution: Duration × (Rewind speed as negative) = Total time change
realworld_examples.application: You've gone back 12 seconds in the video. Positive duration times negative speed gives negative time displacement (going backward in time).
realworld_examples.real_world_relevance: Used in video editing, audio production, playback controls

realworld_examples.title: Removing Penalties (Double Negative)
realworld_examples.scenario: In a game, you had 4 penalties of -5 points each. The referee removes all penalties.
realworld_examples.problem: What is the net change to your score when penalties are removed?
realworld_examples.solution: Removing (negative operation) a penalty (negative value) gives a positive result.
realworld_examples.application: Removing negative items creates a positive effect. This is why (-) × (-) = (+). You gain 20 points by having penalties removed!
realworld_examples.real_world_relevance: Used in game scoring, penalty systems, corrective actions

common_misconceptions.misconception: Two negatives always make a positive
common_misconceptions.correction: This is only true for multiplication and division, not addition or subtraction
common_misconceptions.teaching_strategy: Explicitly compare multiplication vs. addition of negatives

common_misconceptions.misconception: Multiplying by negative always gives negative
common_misconceptions.addressed_in: Learn Mode Pattern 2, Practice Mode Questions 2 & 4
common_misconceptions.teaching_strategy: Use Real World Mode Example 5 (removing penalties) to illustrate

common_misconceptions.correction: Zero is neither positive nor negative
common_misconceptions.teaching_strategy: Emphasize zero as transition point in patterns

common_misconceptions.misconception: Integers aren't used in real life
common_misconceptions.correction: Integers model direction, debt, temperature, elevation, etc.
common_misconceptions.teaching_strategy: Connect each example to students' experiences

common_misconceptions.misconception: Pattern only works with these specific numbers
common_misconceptions.addressed_in: Learn Mode calculator, Practice Mode varied questions
common_misconceptions.teaching_strategy: Encourage testing with different numbers in calculator

Not discussing why patterns work, just what they are
Skipping Real World mode due to time constraints
Not connecting the three modes together in summary
Assuming all students grasp concepts at same pace
